etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Late Latin intellēctus (“understanding, intellect”), perfect passive participle of Latin intellegō (“understand; reason”), from inter (“between, among”) + legō (“read”), with connotation of bind.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The faculty of thinking, judging, abstract reasoning, and conceptual understanding; the cognitive faculty.
(uncountable) The capacity of that faculty (in a particular person).

quote.citation: 1983, “Intelligence”, in Shiver, performed by Virna Lindt:
quote.text: Arms of stripes and shirts of checks / You had a very nice intellect

definitions.definition: A person who has that faculty to a great degree.
